page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.large is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family. Built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates two dedicated vCPUs across a single physical core utilizing hyperthreading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It provides 8.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero GPU accelerators. Networking is defined by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark assessments show the instance placing in lower percentiles across compute and memory workloads. The single-core stress-ng rating registers at 1099.38, while multi-core performance scores 1456.5. Geekbench evaluation reflects similar boundaries, with single-core and multi-core scores reaching 937.0 and 1108.0 respectively. PassMark CPU testing yields 1826.13, and memory throughput benchmarks record 10.45 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 9.47 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-oriented metrics, the configuration achieves 1.48 million Redis SET operations per second, a static web serving rate of 1.26 GB/sec, and 38.09 tokens per second on lightweight 135M-parameter language model generation.

Because of its constrained single-thread and parallel performance metrics, ecs.g5ne.large is best suited for low-load tasks rather than intensive analytical or compilation pipelines. Its resource balance offers a cost-effective platform for running staging containers, basic development tasks, low-volume web services, microservices, and internal monitoring agents where raw compute capacity is secondary to maintaining an active runtime environment.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.large is a general-purpose virtual instance belonging to the Enhanced family. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance provisions two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, while lacking bundled local disk storage and GPU hardware. External block storage must be attached separately for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the instance records lower-tier results across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, reflecting entry-level processing capability and limited memory bandwidth. Small-scale services achieve moderate throughput, such as 1.48 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.26 GB/sec in static web serving. The hardware allocation represents an economical configuration suited for lightweight web serving, minor utility applications, staging, and development environments requiring modest compute and memory.
